newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher, lifted by light hog marketings on Monday and expected light runs on Tuesday, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
Marketings were down as farmers instead started preparing fields for spring planting, sources said.
The light hog movement offset potential weakness from light demand, with several slaughter and processing plants closed in observance of the Easter holiday, the dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen steady at $50.50 to $51.00.
Illinois top prices at the plant were seen ranging $51.50 to $52.00. Indiana/Ohio top plant prices could span $50.50 to $51.00.
Hog prices Tuesday also were seen supported by ideas some hog plants not open on Monday would be competing for available hogs Tuesday, livestock dealers said.
Cash hog price gains could be muted, however, by mostly lower pork prices on Monday, they said.
In its midday carlot pork report, USDA quoted fresh hams down $2.00 to $3.00 per cwt but bellies were steady to $1.00 higher.
